question: Will Donald Trump's approval rating reach a new low in the second half of December 2026?

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin average ~37.0% on Nov 17, 2026, vs. the all-time second-term low of 36.3% (set around late Sep–Oct 2026). Resolving YES needs the average to go below the running minimum during Dec 16-31 specifically. Any new low set between Nov 18 and Dec 15 raises the bar. Random-walk reasoning (monthly SD ~1pt, slight downward drift after the midterms, strong-approve eroding, individual polls at record lows of 30-32%) gives ~45-50% for a new low by year-end, of which only part lands in the final 16-day window. Fewer polls over the holidays slow movement. No matching market: the Manifold 35%-in-2026 market (0.22, low volume) uses a different source and threshold.
calls.dossier:
- Silver Bulletin tracker (natesilver.net, fetched 2026-11-18): Nov 17, 2026 = 37% approve / 60% disapprove; page text: 'After rebounding slightly to 38 percent, Donald Trump's approval rating is back on the downswing.' Strongly approve 18.9%, weakly approve 18.3%.
- All-time low in Silver average: 36.3% (Gabe Fleisher on X; Newsweek, Nov 2026, says 'slightly above its all-time low of 36.3'). Newsweek reported the net-approval record low of -22.4 around Sep 23, 2026. The exact date of the 36.3 low was not confirmed (likely late Sep–Oct 2026).
- Silver Bulletin 37.6% on Nov 12 (Newsweek/Yahoo, mid-Nov 2026); net -22.8 at end of October (Newsweek Oct 29); October saw a +0.5 net recovery.
- Individual polls at record lows mid-Nov 2026: Economist/YouGov 32% (Nov 9-11), Reuters/Ipsos 32% (4th straight; career low 31% mid-Oct), CNN/SSRS 32%, Pew 30%. Other averages: RCP 38.7, NYT 36.
- Context: Democrats won the House and Senate on Nov 3, 2026; Iran war ~9 months old with 31% support; gas prices and inflation concerns.
- Status quo: the average hovers at 36-38.7 since October without a new low.
- Resolves off the 'approve' column in the Silver Bulletin CSV; it must be strictly below every prior second-term value, including any new lows set Nov 18–Dec 15.
- Event window: Dec 16 -> Dec 31, 2026 per the criteria; as of Nov 18, 0% elapsed (window starts in ~28 days).
- Holiday period: polling volume usually drops in late December, so the average moves less.
- Markets: Manifold 'below 35% (538/RCP) in 2026' uses a different source and threshold; no market on this exact question was found.
- Searched but not found: the exact date of the 36.3 low and the CSV values.
calls.reference_class: Probability that a slowly moving presidential approval average ~0.7pt above its all-time low sets a new low within a specific 16-day window starting ~4 weeks out

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin record low is 36.3% (set ~mid-Oct 2026); current level ~37.0-37.3% as of Nov 17 and described as 'back on the downswing'. YES requires the running minimum to be set within Dec 16-31 specifically: any new low before Dec 16 raises the bar. Brownian arcsine heuristic gives ~42% that the 43-day minimum falls in the last 16 days; requiring it to also break 36.3 (~0.8 pts below current, ~1.2pt horizon SD) gives ~25%. calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin's all-time low is ~36.3% (around Oct 21, 2026). The average is now ~37.0-37.6% after sliding back from a ~38% rebound, so it needs to fall ~0.7-1.1 points and set the record specifically in the 16-day Dec 16-31 window. It must also beat any new low set between now and Dec 15. Base rate: the average set new lows roughly every 2-3 months in 2026 (May, Aug, Oct), so a given 16-day window has roughly a 15-25% chance. Pushing up: recent downswing, record-low individual polls (YouGov 32%, Reuters/Ipsos 32%), an unpopular Iran war, the post-midterm slump. Pushing down: holiday polling lull, averages holding around 37-38%, the short window. Markets: no matching contract. A Polymarket 'how low in 2026' market reportedly ~39% on reaching 35% (search snippet, not verified); Manifold 'below 35% 538/RCP in 2026' at 22% on thin volume. Both are near-misses on threshold, window and source.

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin second-term low is ~36.3%; current ~37.0% (Nov 17) and described as trending down. YES needs a new record low set specifically within Dec 16-31, beating any low set Nov 18-Dec 15. With no drift, P(the 43-day minimum dips below 36.3) is ~45-55%. The arcsine law gives ~42% that the minimum falls in the final 16 days, and the two overlap, giving ~0.25. Slight downward drift (record-low individual polls at ~32%, Iran war) is offset by the holiday polling lull and mean reversion.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: record low ~36.3% in the Silver CSV, current ~37.0% (Nov 17), window Dec 16-31, and the bar ratchets down if a low is set before then. Factual disputes: (1) the date of the record low (late Sep / mid-Oct / Oct 21) cannot be settled without web access but does not matter, since only the level does; (2) current level 37.0 vs 37.6 is a date difference, and the Nov 17 page text says ~37%. Judgment: base-rate method (arcsine random walk vs counting 2026 record-setting frequency) gives a similar ~15-30% range either way. I independently re-derived ~0.25 from the arcsine + barrier argument, then added a slight nudge for downward drift and the fact that any reading below the record by any margin counts, offset by the holiday polling lull. Final 0.26.
